summary: Three deterministic defects were found in the frozen source: two EVM execution-state/reporting bugs that can lose track of already-broadcast trades, and one wrapped-base identification bug that can corrupt profit and behaviour classification.

findings.title: EVM SiBot swallows post-broadcast live trade failures and can leave real trades untracked

evidence.detail: The BUY path calls trader.buy(...) and then waits for a receipt, so a real on-chain transaction may already have been broadcast before any later exception is raised.
A blanket `except Exception: continue` drops any receipt/balance/DB failure after the broadcast, so no position row, execution row, or operator-visible failure is recorded.
The LIVE sell path likewise broadcasts `trader.sell(...)` before performing receipt and balance reconciliation.
Leader-triggered sells wrap `close_position(...)` in `except Exception: pass`, so a post-broadcast failure can be silently discarded while the DB still thinks the position is open.

findings.impact: A BUY or SELL can be submitted on-chain and then disappear from bot state if receipt polling, token-balance reconciliation, or persistence fails. That leaves subsequent leader events and monitoring logic free to enter or exit again, creating duplicate exposure, repeated exits, silent balance drift, and misleading Telegram/operator reports.
findings.root_cause: Irreversible live execution is followed by broad exception suppression instead of durable attempt tracking and explicit reconciliation/quarantine states.
findings.corrective_action: Persist a durable attempt/execution record immediately after obtaining the tx hash, never swallow exceptions after a live broadcast, and move ambiguous post-broadcast failures into a reconciliation/quarantine state that blocks duplicate re-entry or re-exit until the transaction is resolved.
tests_required: Add a SiBot BUY test where trader.buy returns a tx hash but receipt polling or token balance reconciliation fails, and assert that the tx hash is persisted and the position is quarantined or marked pending instead of being silently skipped.

Add a leader SELL test where close_position broadcasts a tx and then raises during receipt/accounting, and assert that the position is not left silently OPEN without a recorded pending/reconcile state.

findings.title: AUTO EVM execution records post-broadcast failures as blank-hash REJECTED rows

evidence.detail: The AUTO path calls `trader.execute_cycle(...)` and stores the real broadcast tx hash in `txh` before waiting for a receipt and computing realised P&L.
Any later timeout or accounting failure raises after the trade is already on-chain.
The catch-all error row hard-codes `tx_hash: ""` and `status: "REJECTED"`, discarding the already-known tx hash and making the trade look like it never broadcast.

findings.impact: When a live AUTO route is broadcast but receipt polling, wrapped-balance reconciliation, or fee-accounting fails, the execution log loses the transaction hash and marks the attempt as rejected. Operators cannot reconcile what actually happened, and retry logic or human intervention can submit the same opportunity again even though funds are already in flight.
findings.root_cause: The error path does not preserve the irreversible execution identifier once the trade crosses the broadcast boundary.
findings.corrective_action: Carry the tx hash into all post-broadcast failure paths and record a distinct pending/reconcile status (for example BROADCAST_PENDING or RECEIPT_TIMEOUT) instead of a blank-hash REJECTED row. Any retry logic should key off that durable tx record.
tests_required: Add an AUTO execution test where `execute_cycle` returns a tx hash and `wait_for_transaction_receipt` times out, then assert the audit row keeps the tx hash and enters a non-retry reconciliation status.
Add a test where wrapped-balance or fee-accounting fails after broadcast and assert the execution log still preserves the tx hash for reconciliation.

findings.title: Wrapped-base detection trusts token symbols instead of the configured wrapped-base address

evidence.detail: Wrapped-base inflow/outflow is detected by comparing `symbol.upper()` with `settings.wrapped_base_symbol.upper()` rather than by token address.
The same symbol-based comparison determines which token becomes `wrapped_delta`, `base_token`, and profit proof quality.
Behaviour classification also removes the wrapped asset from route symbols using only the wrapped-base symbol, so symbol collisions propagate into higher-level strategy labels.

findings.impact: Any token whose metadata symbol matches the chain wrapped base (for example a spoofed `WBNB`/`WETH` token) can be mis-treated as the wrapped native asset. That corrupts `profit_evidence`, proof quality, net-profit calculations, and downstream behaviour/copy-leader rankings, which can mislead operators and poison automated strategy selection.
findings.root_cause: The accounting and classification layers rely on non-unique ERC-20 metadata (`symbol`) instead of the canonical configured wrapped-base token address.
findings.corrective_action: Compare tokens against the configured wrapped-base address throughout profit and behaviour analysis, and use symbols only for display. Add regression coverage for same-symbol, different-address tokens.
tests_required: Add a profit-analysis test where a non-wrapped token intentionally uses the wrapped-base symbol and assert the transaction is not classified as wrapped-base profit evidence.
Add a behaviour-classification test proving same-symbol non-base assets are not filtered out of the route as if they were the chain wrapped base.

refusals_or_limits: Read-only audit only: no live trading, deployment, wallet/secret changes, or code fixes were performed.
The audit was anchored to source commit 128fe91d2a0f2095be823d0a11a6f311e5593cfc via commit-pinned inspection of the repository clone.
GitHub Actions metadata was inspected through MCP tooling; the recent workflow run sampled during the audit did not expose failed jobs tied to this report.
